title: Mariner Telecom VPC capacity, TF modules, and phased upgrade brief
content:
Status: draft - working notes for architect+eng sync with Mariner Telecom

Purpose
- Capture initial sizing assumptions, Terraform module callouts, and a minimally invasive upgrade path for Mariner Telecom's VPC/on-prem deployment.
- This is a working brief to align SRE, infra, and solutions eng before the customer workshop on 2025-11-12.

Summary of ask from Mariner
- Single-region VPC with direct-connect to their colo (MIA-2) and egress through their transit gateway.
- Support for latency-sensitive call transcription + realtime summarization and nightly batch embeddings for analytics.
- SLA expectations: 99.9% uptime, p95 < 160ms for small gen tasks, burstable throughput for peak hours (08:00–10:00 local).
- Data residency: customer-managed encryption keys (KMS/HSM) required.

High-level deployment outline (recommended)
- Control plane: Redwood-managed control plane endpoints; customer wants private control plane traffic over VPC peering (proposal: AWS PrivateLink).
- Serving plane: dedicated capacity in customer's VPC made up of: 3 primary inference nodes (p4d-style or equivalent) + 1 hot spare per AZ; expected starting GPU footprint = 12 x A10G-equivalent (equiv to 3 nodes x 4 GPUs) with vertical scale option.
- Edge workers: 2 smaller CPU-only nodes for batching and pre/post processing (for streaming aggregation).
- Storage: EFS or equivalent for shared model artifacts; S3 compatible object store for cold model storage.
- Networking: ENI-based attachments, 25 Gbps inter-node links recommended; internal LB (NLB) + Envoy sidecars for routing and observability hooks.

Sizing assumptions & rationale
- Traffic profile: 50 qps baseline; 250 qps 5-10 minute bursts during peak; median prompt size 60 tokens, median response 120 tokens.
- Throughput compute model: for the model family they selected (redwood-7b-quantized variant), we measured ~14 tokens/sec/GPU under our runtime in benchmark suite. Using continuous batching heuristics, estimated steady-state token throughput per GPU = 600–700 tokens/sec under typical mixes.
- Node count calculation: baseline demand (50 qps * 180 tokens total => 9k tokens/sec) => ~13 GPUs. We propose an initial conservative allocation of 12 GPUs with autoscale policy + scheduled capacity for peak windows.
- Memory: KV cache sizing to support 8192 context for 12 concurrent long sessions; reserve 30% headroom for model updates.

Terraform module notes (callout items)
- Module naming: use modules/private-inference/vpc, modules/private-inference/serving, modules/private-inference/kms, modules/private-inference/monitoring. Keep module outputs standardized: cluster_id, asg_ids, subnet_ids, security_group_ids.
- Variables: accept lists for azs, instance_types, gpu_count_per_asg, model_registry_s3_path, kms_key_arn (string), control_plane_endpoint (string).
- State: remote state must be stored in customer's S3 bucket with encryption; recommend locking via DynamoDB. Provide a terraform wrapper script that injects role assumption details for customer CI.
- Idempotency: ensure modules include lifecycle ignore_changes for autoscaling desired_count during runtime rolling; rotate only when explicit var trigger.
- Example snippet we plan to provide to Mariner (in brief):
  module "mariner-serving" {
    source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deployments.git//modules/private-inference/serving?ref=mariner-2025-11"
    azs = ["us-east-1a","us-east-1b"]
    instance_types = ["g5.2xlarge","g5.4xlarge"]
    gpu_count_per_asg = 4
    model_registry_s3_path = "s3://mariner-models/redwood/"
    kms_key_arn = var.kms_key_arn
  }

Upgrade plan (minimally disruptive phases)
- Goals: preserve customer SLAs, keep control-plane changes to a minimum, allow rollback to previous runtime within 30 minutes.
- Phase 0 (preflight, 1–2 days): inventory current AMIs, kernel versions, NVIDIA drivers, and runtime dependencies. Validate current Terraform version and provider plugin list.
- Phase 1 (canary, 1 day): deploy new serving runtime (v2.8) to 1 AZ on a subset of capacity (10% traffic) with model pinning to avoid hidden regressions. Observe latency, GPU utilization, and quality metrics for 24 hours.
- Phase 2 (staged rollout, 2–3 days): expand to 50% capacity across AZs, increase traffic share to 50% with automatic fallback to previous runtime on error.
- Phase 3 (full roll, 1 day): switch remaining capacity, run post-upgrade sweep for config drift and reconcile.
- Rollback: pre-built AMI snapshots and terraform run that sets autoscale groups back to previous launch template. Expected recovery < 30 minutes for node replacement; model cache warmup up to 10–20 minutes.

Open architecture Q&A for Mariner (items to verify in customer workshop)
- Q1: Do they require PrivateLink for control plane only, or do they require fully isolated control plane inside their VPC? (affects network design and ops model)
- Q2: Strict HSM requirement vs. KMS with external key import? Which trusts/bindings are required?
- Q3: Can we rely on customer's existing NAT/egress filtering for model downloads, or should we provide a mirrored artifact repository inside the VPC?
- Q4: Expected retention window for observability traces/metrics (we recommend 30d but enterprise customers sometimes ask for 90+ days).
- Q5: SLDB compliance checklist items (data deletion requests, audit log forwarding) — confirm team or partner to manage.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Underestimated peak burst GPU needs -> mitigation: schedule burst capacity (on-demand reserved) and autoscale with buffer nodes in warmpool.
- Risk: KMS integration adds latency to model load operations -> mitigation: use envelope encryption; cache decrypted keys in HSM-backed KMS proxy with strict TTL.
- Risk: Terraform drift during long-lived autoscale changes -> mitigation: nightly reconcile pipeline with drift alerts and manual approvals for infra changes.

Action items (next 7 days)
- [Owner: Jordan Lee] Pre-fill module call example and create PR to private-deployments repo (target branch: mariner-2025-11).
- [Owner: Priya Nair] Schedule Mariner workshop 2025-11-12 14:00 ET and invite networking/security and platform teams.
- [Owner: Samir Patel] Run benchmark with redwood-7b-quantized on an A10G-equivalent node and post results to linked PR.
- [Owner: Mariner POC] Confirm whether HSM is required or standard KMS acceptable.

Appendix: quick numbers cheat-sheet
- Baseline qps: 50
- Peak qps: 250 (5–10 min bursts)
- Median tokens per request: ~180
- Initial GPU allocation proposed: 12 (with warmpool + autoscale)
- Expected p95 latency target: <160ms small gen tasks

Notes to self / meeting prep bullets
- Bring up warmpool costs vs reserved capacity cost tradeoff (pull numbers from cost model).
- Clarify the customer's acceptance criteria for canary success (latency delta, error rate threshold, quality/regression detection).
- Prepare a short demo of private model push via S3 mirroring and example terraform apply with assume-role.

Unresolved / TODO
- Confirm Mariner's cross-account role naming convention for terraform CI.
- Verify if default subnet size (/24 vs /20) — ask Mariner infra.
- Determine expected growth trajectory (6–12 months) to justify reserve vs burst sizing.

End of draft notes.

-- Jordan
